Text: Q: Why does does sertraline make you sleepy? A: Sertraline can make some people feel sleepy due to its effects on chemicals in the brain, especially in the first days to weeks of treatment. Others experience the opposite problem and develop insomnia instead. Clinical trials suggest that drowsiness, fatigue, and other sleep-related side effects are common, but they are usually mild and often improve as the body adapts to the medication over time.
Q: Does Zoloft (sertraline) cause weight gain? A: Yes, Zoloft (sertraline) can cause weight gain, but for most people the amount is small. In a large 2024 U.S. study, adults who started sertraline gained about half a pound on average after 6 months and about 3 pounds after 2 years. Many people gain no weight at all, and some people, especially children, lose weight.
Triplet: ["sertraline", "has weight gain pattern", "most people gain small amount"]

The relation 'has weight gain pattern' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug is associated with a general pattern of weight change specified by the object entity, which may vary among individuals.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

A. 'has product variation': The subject drug has a different formulation or version specified by the object entity.
B. 'interacts with': The subject drug has a drug interaction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity that may change effects or cause harm.
C. 'used in combination with': The subject drug is used together with the other treatment or lifestyle measure specified by the object entity.
D. 'has inconsistent association with': Studies have shown a variable or unconfirmed link between the subject drug and the condition specified by the object entity.
